paper.title: Algorithm 791: TSHEP2D: Cosine series Shepard method for bivariate interpolation of scattered data

stack: Fortran 77 (TOMS 791 TSHEP2D, single precision Sp; driver1.f, src_792.f, Src/Sp/src.f)

claim.text: Average SSE/SSM over the ten test functions, node set 1, NC 17, NW 30, NR 6, 0.006063 (shipped res1_2), tol_abs 1e-5

values.name: TSHEP2D driver1, node set 1, NC 17, NW 30, NR 6: average SSE/SSM

attempt: Measured in the sandbox, two passes, the same recipe: copy of the unpacked archive, gfortran -std=legacy -w -o ts2tst driver1.f src_792.f ../../Src/Sp/src.f in Drivers/Sp (the PackingList names no compiler: gfortran is ours), run with data1 on stdin. The driver writes its table to res1_2 in the working directory; the shipped res1_2 is deleted from the build copy before each run and is written again by the run in both passes. Pass 1 and pass 2 res1_2 are byte-identical to the shipped res1_2 (average SSE/SSM 0.006063). Printed precision is 6 decimals, so agreement is at the printed value; tol_abs 1e-5.

original_attempt.reason: The PackingList's build (driver1.f, src_792.f, Src) and data1 stdin were followed with gfortran, which the packing list does not name, so the run is partial in the strict sense, as in watson1997-hompack90-777. No step of the authors' procedure failed.
